THE CENSUS NULL-RESULT PATH IS UNREACHABLE, AND TONIGHT'S RUN PROVES IT. Reporting rather than fixing — reasoning at the bottom, and it is not timidity.

THE EVIDENCE, from campaign/the-wicket's census a73d8ce3c9b4, rc=0 in 865 s:

  $ git diff --stat a73d8ce3c9b4..origin/census/a73d8ce3c9b4-20260902T022056Z
    docs/timings.md | 1 +
    1 file changed, 1 insertion(+)

The delivery branch contains ONE path and it is the run's own ledger row. No golden moved. The operator was told 'Goldens delivered on a census/* branch', and CLAUDE.md's documented behaviour — 'A run that moves nothing pushes no branch and says so — a null is a result' — did not happen and CANNOT happen.

THE MECHANISM, and both halves are individually right (scripts/sluice-census.sh:77-90):

  git add -A -- book/src/laboratory/    # stage goldens
  git add -u                            # ALSO sweeps docs/timings.md's census row
  if git diff --cached --quiet; then    # 'NO GOLDENS MOVED' ... unreachable
      echo 'sluice-census: NO GOLDENS MOVED — nothing to deliver.'

The  is deliberate and the comment above it explains why: timed.sh resolves its ledger with a bare /home/nathan/Projects/hornvale, so inside the census worktree the row lands THERE, and this sweep is the only thing that commits it. Narrowing it would reopen the exact bug The Governor's Task 7 fixed for heavy — 27 heavy runs between 2026-08-05 and 2026-08-28 wrote a row nothing ever committed.

So the fix for one bug silently killed a documented behaviour of another. Nothing is wrong with either half on its own.

WHAT IT COSTS. Not corruption — the delivered branch is harmless. It costs INFORMATION: 'the census agrees with your ref' is a genuinely valuable answer and it can no longer be given. And the 'N path(s) moved' line counts STAGED PATHS, so it reports 1 when the true golden count is 0, which reads as movement.

FOR campaign/the-wicket SPECIFICALLY, because this is your actual result and it is a good one: YOUR CENSUS MOVED NOTHING. You changed windows/lab/src/health.rs and windows/lab/src/synthetic.rs, which metrics.rs references in 9 places, so a census was genuinely owed — a census measures the world THROUGH the metric code and changing that code invalidates the prior run. It was the right call to request it. The answer is that the world still agrees: no golden moved. That is a null, and a null is a result. The delivery branch you were pointed at carries only a timings row, so there is nothing to merge for goldens' sake; do not read the branch's existence as evidence your change moved the world, because it is not.

WHY I AM NOT FIXING IT AT 02:30 WITH NO REVIEWER, and this is the actual argument. The failure modes are asymmetric. The bug today OVER-delivers: a branch exists that need not, which is noise. A wrong fix UNDER-delivers: a census with real golden movement gets classified as null, no branch is pushed, and the goldens are silently lost — and the run costs ~865 s to reproduce. Over-delivery is recoverable by reading a diff; under-delivery is a lost measurement nobody knows to look for. When one direction is noise and the other is silent data loss, an unreviewed 02:30 change to the dispatch path is the wrong instrument.

THE SHAPE A FIX SHOULD HAVE, for whoever takes it: the predicate must ask whether anything OUTSIDE docs/timings.md is staged, not whether anything is staged. Both branches then need positive controls, and the load-bearing one is the null — force a census whose goldens genuinely do not move and watch it decline to push, because that is the arm that is dead today and a silent arm is indistinguishable from a working one. That is the same trap the vet's collision check had this evening: it printed nothing on the live case, correctly, and only became evidence once the effect was forced.
